::: {.callout-note title="Pre-Approved Datasets: Our Selection Criteria" collapse="true"}

Looking at a dataset of all [H1-B visa job registrations](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/eta/foreign-labor/performance) submitted by US employers to the Department of Labor, the top industries (by share of total postings per [NAICS code](https://www.naics.com/search/)) hiring **data scientists** specifically (OES Code [15-2051](https://www.bls.gov/oes/2025/may/oes_stru.htm)) are:

| Rank | Industry Group | NAICS Code | Percent |
|:-:|:- |:-| -:|
| 1 | Tech Companies | [5415](https://www.naics.com/code-search/?trms=5415&v=2022&styp=naics&qid=5aeae87a70) | 21.44% |
| 2 | Banking and Finance | [52](https://www.naics.com/code-search/?trms=52&v=2022&styp=naics&qid=5aeae87a70) | 7.95% |
| 3 | Retail Sales | [45](https://www.naics.com/code-search/?trms=45&v=2022&styp=naics&qid=5aeae87a70) | 7.72% |
| 4 | Consulting Firms | [5416](https://www.naics.com/code-search/?trms=5416&v=2022&styp=naics&qid=5aeae87a70) | 4.01% |
| 5 | Scientific Research Labs | [5417](https://www.naics.com/code-search/?trms=5417&v=2022&styp=naics&qid=5aeae87a70) | 2.58% |
| 6 | Healthcare Organizations | [62](https://www.naics.com/code-search/?trms=62&v=2022&styp=naics&qid=5aeae87a70) | 2.06% |

Thus, in choosing datasets for the midterm, my aim was to cover the **types of data you might encounter** working as a data scientist / engineer within each of these (admittedly very broadly-defined) areas!

One implication of this approach is that, although some of the data is *historical* (like the Enron Email Corpus), the goal will **not** be just to analyze this nicely-packaged self-contained datasets, but instead to imagine **how you would handle *new* data continuously streaming into an OLTP database** with the same structure! So, in the Enron Email Corpus example, your interest won't be in analyzing those emails in particular, but to use them as a **case study**, extrapolating how you might use the tools we've learned in class thus far to derive analytic insights from a hypothetical employer's email database.

:::

## Overview

Starting **after the Midterm**, and up through the **presentations** on December 7th and December 10th and **reports** due on December 13th, you will apply the skills you've learned in the course towards a **Final Project**.

### Dataset Choice

Note that, as indicated by the **"pre-approved"** qualifier on the datasets listed below, you **do not need to restrict yourself** to only these datasets! We encourage you to choose a dataset and topic that you are particularly interested in, as long as they meet the general requirements described in class at the beginning of [Week 10](../w10/index.qmd).

Projects using datasets outside of the "pre-approved" list will just need to describe these datasets in the [Proposal](#proposal-due-sunday-november-15-2026) document, as described in that section below.

### Individual vs. Group Projects

Projects can be done **individually** or in **groups** of between 2 and 4 students. The only differences between individual and group projects are as follows:

* **Expectations** in terms of the **work** carried out as part of a project will be **scaled** based on the size of the group: a group with 4 members will be expected to carry out 2x more work than a group with 2 members.
* **Final Presentation times** will also be scaled according to group size, as described in the next paragraph.

Course staff will **recalculate the number of minutes per presentation** (based on the distribution of groups this semester) once the [**Proposals**](#proposal-due-sunday-november-15-2026) have been submitted, but last semester the timing worked out as follows:

| Group Size | Presentation Time Limit |
|:-:| - |
| 1 | 5 minutes |
| 2 | 8 minutes |
| 3 | 10 minutes |
| 4 | 12 minutes |

### Deliverables

The ultimate deliverable (on top of the progress reports and Final Presentation) will be a **Final Report**, due by **11:59pm, Sunday, December 13, 2026**. The report is described in more detail [below](#final-report-due-sunday-december-13-2026), but the format should be a **Quarto Manuscript Page** hosted on **GitHub Pages**, and thus accessible to course staff via a URL like `gh_username.github.io/project-name`.

## Final Project Roadmap

If you go to a conference or summit or some similar kind of gathering in the "computational sciences" world (computer science, data science, applied math, engineering, etc.), like a [conference sponsored by the IEEE](https://www.ieee.org/conferences-events), you will find that the organizational structure is often based on a split between an **"industry track"** and an **"academic track"**. By the same logic, it might help you to think about whether you would submit your DSAN 6000 Final Project to an "industry track" or an "academic track".

The main reason for mentioning this dual-track setup, however, is to point out that there are **shared standards** across the two tracks: for example, both would require **abstracts** providing 300-500 word descriptions of the projects, and both would have constraints on how long each presenter will be able to speak.

Thus, whether your **goal** in carrying out your project is:

* More oriented towards a "product", with (e.g.) a proof-of-concept demonstration forming the core of the final presentation, or
* More oriented towards a "scientific finding", e.g., using big healthcare data to machine-learn likely indicators of allgergies to certain medications,

The following **weekly milestones** are meant to provide the "conference organizers" (the course staff) with progress updates, so that we can help you bring the projects to fruition given the time and resources we have available between now and the week of December 7th!

### Proposal: Due *Sunday, November 15, 2026*

<center>

[Canvas submission link]({{< var project.proposal-url >}})

</center>

The initial proposal is a 1-to-2-page document, due by 11:59pm, Sunday, November 15, 2026 on **Canvas**, which should include the following:

1.  **Name(s)** of who will work on the project,
2.  **Dataset(s)** that will be utilized in the project (see [Dataset Choice Details](#dataset-choice-details) below),
3.  **Preliminary "extended abstract"** describing the goals of the project (here you can use the structure of the Midterm vignettes as a guide), and
4.  **(Optional) Questions for course staff**, where you can include anything you'd like us to address to help you before you start working on the project.

#### Dataset Choice Details

As described in the [Overview](#overview) section, you **do not need to use** one of the "pre-approved" datasets! We encourage you to choose anything you are particularly interested in that meets the general requirements described in class at the beginning of [Week 10](../w10/index.qmd).

The only difference, therefore, is that projects using a non-"pre-approved" dataset will need to describe the dataset in this Proposal document. Please write your description so that the course staff has a sense for the **scale** and **feasibility** of applying course tools to the dataset – for example, you can copy the structure used in the Midterm vignettes, including an indication of **where** exactly the dataset can be accessed (say, an S3 bucket URI like `s3://data-bucket/specific-dataset/`).

<center>

[Canvas submission link]({{< var project.report-url >}})

</center>

The Final Report, as described in class during [Week 11](../w11/index.qmd), should be structured as a **Quarto Manuscript** page hosted on **GitHub Pages**, with an easily-accessible URL like `gh_username.github.io/project-name`. You (or your group leader) will then **submit this URL** to the above Canvas page.

A **PDF-formatted version of the report** should be **easily accessible** to course staff at that URL: for example, within the **"Other Formats"** section that Quarto automatically includes in the page header for multi-format Manuscript projects.

If you have privacy concerns, and don't want the report to be publicly-accessible at a URL like this, please **email the instructional staff at** [**`dsan6000@georgetown.edu`**](mailto:dsan6000@georgetown.edu) to obtain approval for a PDF-upload-only Final Report submission.
